response:
READING

**Fixed costs: same either way**
The 28-extra-remakes-per-technician figure totalling GBP 27,072 sits under both courses identically. No decision here turns on it.

**KIRKBANE's incremental costs**
One item: GBP 44,000 overtime. In exchange the laboratory gets a clean cut—no dual shade libraries, no mid-case system hops, all technicians learning together.

**AVENSWOOD's incremental costs**

*Crossing remakes.* The pilot is the only hard evidence. Two technicians on the new system for four months alongside ten on Kessendale produced 40 crossing remakes. That is ten crossing remakes per month of dual-system operation.

AVENSWOOD runs two systems for nine months. If the crossing-remake rate scaled purely by time, that is 90 remakes × GBP 96 = GBP 8,640. To test whether mixing intensity matters I can weight each phase by the product of technicians on each system (a proxy for handoff probability):

| Phase | New / Old | Mixing index | Months | Weighted unit-months |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan–Apr 2027 | 3 / 7 | 21 | 3 | 63 |
| Apr–Jul 2027 | 6 / 4 | 24 | 3 | 72 |
| Jul–Oct 2027 | 9 / 1 | 9 | 3 | 27 |
| **Total** | | | | **162** |

Pilot: 2 × 10 = 20 mixing-index × 4 months = 80 unit-months → 40 remakes, or 0.50 remakes per unit-month. Applying that: 162 × 0.50 ≈ 81 crossing remakes × GBP 96 ≈ **GBP 7,776**.

The two methods bracket one another. A reasonable point estimate is GBP 8,000–9,000 in crossing remakes; even a pessimistic doubling gives GBP 16,000–18,000.

*Shade library and material library duplication.* The pilot did not report shade-confusion remakes as a separate category; only crossing remakes were noted. The risk is real but not evidenced at a rate that approaches the overtime figure. At GBP 96 per remake, erasing a GBP 35,000 advantage would require ~365 shade-confusion remakes over nine months—roughly 41 a month—a rate unsupported by anything in the pilot.

**Net financial comparison**

| | KIRKBANE | AVENSWOOD |
|---|---|---|
| Overtime | GBP 44,000 | — |
| Crossing remakes | — | ~GBP 8,500 |
| Library confusion | — | modest, unquantified |
| **Net additional over fixed** | **~GBP 44,000** | **~GBP 8,500–18,000** |

AVENSWOOD saves roughly GBP 25,000–35,000 on quantified items.

**Quality signal to practices**

Under KIRKBANE, all 40 practices receive elevated remake rates in the same calendar month. Even with proactive communication, forty practices simultaneously experiencing worse outcomes creates concentrated reputational exposure and a shared data point they may compare with one another. Under AVENSWOOD, at any point the majority of the bench is at or near the settled 3.1% rate, so most orders for most practices clear normally throughout the transition.

**Timeline against deadline**

KIRKBANE: all crossed by 2027-12-04 (18 months buffer to EOL).
AVENSWOOD: last technician onto new system by 2027-10-04 (20 months buffer to EOL). Both are safe. The deadline is not a swing factor.

**Team learning**

KIRKBANE offers all-hands collective learning, which has real value. AVENSWOOD offers cohort learning in groups of three. The pilot pair demonstrates that learning in a small group works; the difference here is not decisive.

**Summary of decision logic**

KIRKBANE's single concrete saving is GBP 44,000 in overtime. Against that, AVENSWOOD's crossing-remake penalty is bounded by pilot observation at roughly GBP 8,500, and shade confusion is not evidenced at scale. The net financial advantage of AVENSWOOD is around GBP 25,000–35,000 on quantities that can actually be estimated. On quality, AVENSWOOD buffers practice relationships better by never concentrating the learning-curve spike across all 40 practices at once. The dual-library complexity is real but nine months long and manageable with clear labelling and practice communication. There is no scenario in the data where KIRKBANE's costs come out lower.

---

READING
  The pilot measured 40 crossing remakes in four months of dual-system operation; scaled to AVENSWOOD's nine-month window that is roughly GBP 8,500 in extra remakes—well below the GBP 44,000 overtime AVENSWOOD avoids—and AVENSWOOD also keeps three-quarters of the bench at the settled 3.1% rate throughout, sparing most practices from the concentrated spike that KIRKBANE delivers to all forty in the same month.

CALL
  AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
  The overtime saving under AVENSWOOD (GBP 44,000) is four to five times the crossing-remake penalty that the pilot data support (~GBP 8,500), and the staggered approach protects practice relationships by ensuring most bench output stays at the settled remake rate throughout the transition.
